newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Telia's discussing privatisation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Telia's discussing privatisation - paper.

text.p: Sweden's national telephone operator Telia was holding continuing discussions about privatisation, the company's chairman Bengt Westerberg told Swedish financial daily Dagens Industri on Wednesday.
"The issue is being considered," Westerberg said.

"The owner, the government, has still not dismissed privatisation and listing of Telia. But I don't think we will get an answer on the issue until the telecommunications proposal is presented at the beginning of March."
According to its business plan, Telia will enter the media business and start expanding abroad, the newspaper said.

To do this and to compensate for falling revenue when prices fall following stronger competition and new technology, the company needs a capital injection of 5-10 billion crowns ($675-$1.3 billion), the newspaper said.

In December, Transport & Communications Minister Ines Uusman dismissed the idea of listing Telia, but lately she has said Telia should have the same prerequisites as other European telephone operators active in the same markets.
Many of those operators are listed or on the starting blocks to become listed, the newspaper said.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 7.415 Swedish Crowns)
